```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "1 / 1")
```

The fixture for Typst locators under a page numbering of its own (M099). The
raw Typst block above sets the pattern `1 / 1`, which names two counters, so
each page's footer prints the page counter's value there and its final value.
The block is raw Typst rather than the `page-numbering:` key because the
Typst template of Quarto 1.5.52 sets the numbering `1` and ignores that key.
The block comes before any text, and the document has no title, so it starts
no page of its own. Raw Typst blocks change the pattern and reset the page
counter below.

Every page ends where the next one starts: at an explicit page break, or at a
raw Typst `set page` rule, which starts a new page itself. So the physical
page each mark sits on is a fact of this source, and the suite's manifest
states every page from here and nowhere else. Each term is marked in one case
of its own, so no two cases share an entry.

## Physical page 1

The page counter is 1, and the pattern is `1 / 1`.

A term marked here and again after the reset prints one locator:
[apple]{.index}.

A range opens here and closes after the reset, on a page that prints the same
text: [birch]{.index range="open"}.

A term marked here and marked as principal after the reset prints one bold
locator: [cedar]{.index}.

The first of two ranges with the same end texts opens here:
[dune]{.index range="open"}.

A range that opens and closes on this page sits beside a mark after the reset
that prints the same text: [elm]{.index range="open"} and
[elm]{.index range="close"}.

A term marked here, on the next page and after the reset prints the text of
this page first, where its earliest mark sits: [kale]{.index}.

A range opens here and closes on the next page, which a mark inside the
range shares, and a mark after the reset prints that page's text again:
[lime]{.index range="open"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Physical page 2

The page counter is 2.

A mark between the pages of the range of `birch`, which prints one text and
so spans nothing: [birch]{.index}.

The first range of `dune` closes here: [dune]{.index range="close"}.

A range opens here and closes after the reset, on a page that prints a lower
number: [fern]{.index range="open"}. A mark on the range's opening page,
which that range does not span: [fern]{.index}.

The second mark of `kale`: [kale]{.index}.

The range of `lime` closes here, beside a mark inside it:
[lime]{.index range="close"} and [lime]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

```{=typst}
#counter(page).update(1)
```

## Physical page 3

The page counter is reset to 1 on this page.

The second mark of `apple`: [apple]{.index}.

The range of `birch` closes here: [birch]{.index range="close"}.

The principal mark of `cedar`: [cedar]{.index mention="principal"}.

The second range of `dune` opens here: [dune]{.index range="open"}.

The mark of `elm`: [elm]{.index}.

The range of `fern` closes here: [fern]{.index range="close"}.

The third mark of `kale`: [kale]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Physical page 4

The page counter is 2.

The second range of `dune` closes here: [dune]{.index range="close"}.

The mark of `lime` that prints the text of the page inside its range:
[lime]{.index}.

A term marked here and on the next page, where the counter is also 2 under
another pattern, prints two locators: [holly]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "i of I")
#counter(page).update(2)
```

## Physical page 5

The pattern is `i of I`, which names two counters, and the page counter is
reset to 2 again.

A mark under this pattern: [gorse]{.index}.

The second mark of `holly`: [holly]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "- 1 -")
```

## Physical page 6

The pattern is `- 1 -`, which names one counter, and the page counter is 3.

A mark under this pattern: [iris]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: none)
```

## Physical page 7

This page has no numbering, and the page counter is 4.

A mark on a page with no numbering: [juniper]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "1 / 1")
```
